name: Temazepam
lead: Temazepam is a prescription benzodiazepine hypnotic used for short-term treatment of insomnia, sold in the US under the brand name Restoril. It enhances the action of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA at GABA-A receptors, producing sedation, and is a Schedule IV controlled substance in the United States.[1][2]

In looksmaxxing and physique circles, its relevance runs through sleep. Sleep is where training recovery, growth hormone release and skin repair are generally said to happen, so people who struggle to sleep (for example while using stimulating hormones or anabolic compounds) sometimes discuss prescription sleep aids as a way to protect that recovery and, indirectly, their training progress and skin and eye appearance.[20][17][19] The chain is indirect: better sleep, better recovery, more consistent training and a more rested look.

Research on temazepam is about sleep: sleep latency, total sleep time, next-day effects, dependence and safety in older adults.[3][4][7] No published trial has tested it for appearance outcomes. Regulators and guideline bodies describe it as a short-term treatment and attach boxed warnings about dependence and combination with opioids.[2][3]

paras: The US label indicates temazepam for short-term treatment of insomnia, generally seven to ten days, and notes that the efficacy trials supporting approval lasted two weeks.[2] The American Academy of Sleep Medicine guideline for chronic insomnia reviewed it among individual drugs, and cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia is recommended first-line by sleep societies, with drugs as an adjunct.[3][11] A review of insomnia treatment in older adults lists temazepam and triazolam as the FDA-approved benzodiazepines for insomnia and discusses their benefits and harms in that age group.[11]

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and physique communities
paras: Posts on the bodybuilding forum T Nation show temazepam mentioned as a sleep aid by people on testosterone therapy or other hormonal regimens. One user reports a physician prescribing it for sleeplessness on TRT, another describes taking it for lifelong sleep problems, and a third says insomnia from aromatase inhibitors and hormones led a doctor to prescribe it with trazodone.[17][18][19] In a discussion of an anabolic cycle, one poster says a friend was tempted to use it to sleep while on trenbolone, and another says a source of theirs had it.[20][21]
Users generally frame it as a sleep tool rather than an appearance tool. Others in the same threads mention alternatives such as melatonin, diphenhydramine or mirtazapine.[17][18][22]

Temazepam is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor, increasing the inhibitory effect of GABA and reducing neuronal excitability, which produces sedation, anxiolysis and muscle relaxation.[1] It is taken orally, with near-complete absorption, peak blood levels after about two to three hours and a terminal half-life that Wikipedia puts at roughly 8 to 20 hours.[10] It is metabolised in the liver, chiefly by conjugation, and excreted mostly in urine.[10]
Sleep-laboratory work has found that temazepam can suppress slow-wave sleep at higher doses even while increasing total sleep time.[1]

In the controlled studies summarised on the US label, 1,076 patients received temazepam. Drowsiness (9.1 percent versus 5.6 percent on placebo), dizziness, lethargy and next-day hangover were more frequent than with placebo, while headache and nervousness were similar or less frequent.[2] Anterograde amnesia, slowed reaction time and impaired coordination are described in the pharmacology literature.[1][10]

The label carries a boxed warning: combining benzodiazepines with opioids can cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death, and the class carries risks of abuse, misuse, addiction, dependence and withdrawal reactions.[2] A BMJ case-cohort study of US veterans receiving opioid analgesics linked benzodiazepine prescribing patterns to overdose deaths.[5] The FDA required an updated boxed warning across the benzodiazepine class in September 2020.[10] Older adults show increased sensitivity, and use is not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding.[1][7][10]
The label also warns about combining sedatives with other central nervous system depressants, including alcohol.[2]

Wikipedia dates the compound's patent to 1962, with medical use beginning in 1969 in the article's introduction and 1981 in its history section, a discrepancy the article does not resolve; Grokipedia describes synthesis in the 1960s and international marketing from the 1970s.[10][1] By the late 1980s it was widely prescribed as a hypnotic.[10]

In 1980s and 1990s Britain, the liquid-filled gel capsules were misused by injection, and temazepam was described as the most widely abused legal prescription drug in the UK in 1987; street names included jellies.[10] Drug deaths in Glasgow and Edinburgh in 1990 to 1992 were linked to heroin combined with temazepam, diazepam and alcohol, and a BBC Panorama episode covered the problem.[10] A 1978 Lancet report had observed that chewed capsules acted faster than swallowed ones, an early hint of how the formulation could be exploited.[13] Several jurisdictions responded with regulation: Finland withdrew a liquid-capsule product, Australia withdrew capsules in March 2004 and left only tablets, and France withdrew a brand in 2013.[10]

Temazepam is Schedule IV in the United States and Canada, Class C under the UK Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 with a special prescription form for private prescriptions, Schedule 4 in Australia, Schedule 3 in Ireland, Class A in Norway and banned in Sweden.[10]

A JAMA randomised trial compared behavioural and pharmacological therapy, including temazepam, for late-life insomnia.[4] The AASM guideline reviewed temazepam among drugs for chronic insomnia, and published summaries describe reduced time to fall asleep and increased total sleep time versus placebo.[3][1] A 2006 military trial examined temazepam and zaleplon for inducing afternoon sleep.[14] A 2024 randomised trial of masked tapering with behavioural therapy enrolled adults aged 55 and older who had used temazepam or other sleep medications, testing how to discontinue them.[12] A 1979 sleep-laboratory study evaluated its long-term hypnotic efficacy.[15]

Registered trials have examined temazepam at high altitude and in insomnia among people with HIV.[8][9] A matched cohort study associated hypnotic use with higher mortality; observational designs cannot show causation.[6] No studies of appearance outcomes were found.

card.summary: A prescription benzodiazepine sleeping pill; sleep research only, no appearance data.
card.note: Schedule IV; dependence risk, dangerous with opioids or alcohol.

quick.overview:
Temazepam is a prescription benzodiazepine used for short-term insomnia.

No research links it to appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: It enhances the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA at GABA-A receptors, causing sedation.
quick.risks: Reported risks include drowsiness, amnesia, tolerance, dependence and withdrawal, and serious respiratory depression when combined with opioids or alcohol. Schedule IV in the US.

angle.text: People who use it, on prescription, to treat insomnia describe it as a way to get enough sleep when stimulants, hormones or stress interfere. Any effect on looks runs through sleep and recovery rather than a direct action on skin, fat or muscle.
